Closest pre-existing call, re-verified live: chunk 5 line 42 'the second-pass read' is not named verbatim anywhere earlier in THIS file's own prose (grepped raw lines 1-41 for 'second-pass|second read': zero hits) — but `grep -in 'second-pass\|second read' curriculum/exercises/push-back-on-the-plan.md` run live this pass returns 7 hits (lines 5, 62, 68, 77, 111, 117, 123: 'a second-pass grilling', "it is the second-pass read's job", 'The second read runs in this same session...', 'the second read asks three questions at a time', 'what the second-pass read surfaced', 'The second read catches...', 'shaped by two different reads'). That exercise is linked at chunk 4 line 32 (`[Exercise: Push back on the plan]`), delivered by module include-order directly before this chunk, per `check_slides.md`'s own stated inheritance direction ('module include-order = deck order... vocabulary the enclosing module file's signposting introduced... counts as prior context for the exercises... it includes' — read here symmetrically for the reverse direction, a closer immediately following the exercise it names, matching the spirit of the 'module-arc beats in openers/closers' carve-out even though that carve-out's literal wording names lectures). A reader reaching chunk 5 has just lived the exercise that defines the term five separate ways; 'Walk down unresolved branches' (chunk 3, What You'll Learn) independently telegraphs the same concept before the exercise even runs. Stays inside. Chunk 5 lines 46-50 pronouns (it/them/the old ones) resolve within the same paragraph chain to './CLAUDE.local.md' (named line 42). Chunk 6 lines 54-60 ('your file', 'these', 'it') resolve to CLAUDE.local.md (chunk 5) and the chunk's own three bullets. Chunk 7 line 72 'the deferred ones' resolves via same-bullet ellipsis to 'decisions'. No never-named, vague-with-history, or re-chunk-stranded referent found.

New da Costa paragraph (chunk 9, lines 95-97): 'Module 4 sends off a session that runs without you watching, which is where you meet that limit yourself' names Module 4 by number and unpacks its claim in the same sentence — not a positional pointer, same shape the chunk's own M3 branch already uses ('the security frame Module 3 works in'). (b) Anaphora/epistrophe triples — none; closest candidate is chunk 6's three bullets (Planning gaps/Conflicting information/Other context), which open with distinct handles and distinct content, not a refrain. (c) Self-grading superlatives — `grep -inE 'one of the (most|best)|most useful|most important|extremely useful'` over body run live: zero matches. New paragraph carries no number. (f) Verb triplets with an empty leg — none found; the five What-You'll-Learn LO verbs (chunk 3) are a template-mandated list, not a triplet-tic construction.

Harm check: compared live against this SAME chunk's module:earn-the-trust branch (raw line 101, two sentences, compliant) and against `earn-the-trust.md`'s own `## Next` (raw lines 104-106, ~50 words, no sizing criteria or worked examples — states what M4 does and what the student carries, then one optional pointer) — the corpus norm is short and non-teaching; this branch is 2-3x longer and does the exact teaching the rule bans. The maintainer accept-note at raw line 137 covers only the BOLD-emphasis question on this same passage ('A slides judge reads either as a §9 emphasis-budget violation... Accepted-by-design') — it is silent on sentence count / teaching content, so it does not cover this finding. The obvious blunt fix (delete the criteria and examples) would degrade the artefact by removing task-sizing guidance this cut has nowhere else to deliver it — UNLESS relocated rather than cut: chunk 9's sibling 'Pre-reads before Module 4' branch (same flag, immediately prior chunk, currently only 73 words) is a ready, compliant home, matching how the module:earn-the-trust cut keeps its own task-sizing content in 'Pre-reads before Module 3' and out of 'Next'.

rule_questions: Rule 9's stated multi-bold carve-outs are the §34 task-sizing whole-sentence exception and the reading-list/menu/lookup-surface waiver; it does not explicitly say a plain checklist slide (not a menu, not a law/consolidation slide) may carry one short handle per item. Chunk 6 ('Leave the repo tidier than you found it') bolds three ≤2-word checklist-item names (Planning gaps / Conflicting information / Other context), which this pass reads as compliant under the rule's own 'checklist item names' handle-definition clause rather than under either named carve-out. Worth a maintainer confirmation that a plain 3-item checklist with short handles is intended to clear the ≤1-per-slide default the same way a menu slide does, so a future judge doesn't file it as three-bolds-on-one-slide.
